**To:** Supervising Partner  
**From:** Senior Associate  
**Date:** 28 December 2026  
**Matter:** Eskdale Energy plc acquisition of Juniper Technologies Ltd  
**Client:** Eskdale Energy plc (Buyer)  
**Counterparty:** Quayside Foods Ltd (Seller)  
**Target:** Juniper Technologies Ltd (Company)

- **High Risk:** Closing scheduled 80 days before merger clearance, creating regulatory non-compliance and termination risk

**Business Day Definition:** Not defined in SPA. Default to English jurisdiction standard: any day other than Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in England.

| Closing Date | 26 Jan 2027 | Tuesday | 26 Jan 2027 (Business Day) | 29 days | 55 days from 2 Dec 2026 | Inclusive (payment due) | Binding | Failure to pay Purchase Price = breach |

**Discrepancies Identified:**

2. Conditions Deadline (2 Mar 2027) precedes Merger Clearance by 45 days - **CRITICAL**

## Timing Issues Analysis

### Critical Timing Conflict
**Issue:** Closing Date precedes merger clearance by 80 days  
**Source:** [client_email.md] lines 9, [share_purchase_agreement.md] line 31  
**Direct Quote:** 
- "Regulatory counsel has advised that merger clearance is expected by 16 April 2027." (client_email.md line 9)
- "Closing Date means 26 January 2027" (share_purchase_agreement.md line 31)

**Calculation Verification:**
- Agreement Date: 2 December 2026 (Wednesday)
- Closing Date: 26 January 2027 (Tuesday) 
- Merger Clearance Date: 16 April 2027 (Friday)
- Days from Closing to Merger Clearance: 80 days
- Days from Deliverable Date (28 Dec 2026) to Closing: 29 days
- Days from Deliverable Date to Merger Clearance: 109 days

**Risk Rating:** High  
**Legal/Commercial Risk:** Transaction cannot close without merger clearance under English merger control regulations. Proceeding with Closing before clearance constitutes regulatory non-compliance with potential penalties, invalidation risk, and termination rights for both parties.

**Recommended Action:** 
1. Amend SPA to make merger clearance a Condition Precedent to Closing
2. Extend Closing Date to at least 5 Business Days after expected merger clearance date (post-21 April 2027)
3. Add regulatory condition precedent language to Clause 4.1

**Proposed Amendment:**
```
Clause 4.1: Add new sub-clause (d):
(d) all required merger control and regulatory approvals, including but not limited to clearance from the Competition and Markets Authority, shall have been obtained and shall remain in full force and effect.
```

### Conditions Precedent Deadline
**Issue:** Conditions deadline (2 March 2027) also precedes merger clearance  
**Source:** [share_purchase_agreement.md] lines 63-71  
**Direct Quote:** "The obligations of the parties under this Agreement are subject to the satisfaction or waiver by the Buyer of the following conditions (the "Conditions") on or before the date falling 90 days after the date of this Agreement" (lines 63-64)

**Calculation Verification:**
- Agreement Date: 2 December 2026
- 90 days after Agreement: 2 March 2027 (Tuesday)
- Days from Deliverable Date to Conditions Deadline: 64 days
- Days from Conditions Deadline to Merger Clearance: 45 days

**Risk Rating:** High

**Recommended Action:** Extend Conditions deadline to at least 30 days after expected merger clearance date.

**Proposed Amendment:**

Clause 4.1: Replace "on or before the date falling 90 days after the date of this Agreement" with "on or before the date falling 30 days after the date on which all required merger control clearances have been obtained".
```

- If merger clearance obtained on 16 April 2027 (expected)
- 30 days after: 16 May 2027 (Sunday)
- Adjusted to next Business Day: 17 May 2027 (Monday)
- Days from Deliverable Date: 140 days
- Days from original Conditions Deadline (2 Mar 2027): 76 days extension

## Contractual Inconsistencies and Ambiguities

### Interpretive Ambiguities

#### Ambiguity 1: "Material Contract" Definition
**Source:** [disclosure_letter.md] line 12, [share_purchase_agreement.md] implied reference  
**Direct Quote:** "Material Contracts" has the meaning given in Warranty 6.3 of the SPA" (disclosure_letter.md line 12)

**Alternative Interpretations:**
1. **Narrow Interpretation:** Only contracts meeting specific financial thresholds (e.g., >£X value) are Material Contracts
2. **Broad Interpretation:** Any contract material to the Company's business, including key customer relationships regardless of value

**Legal/Commercial Consequences:**
- **Narrow:** Material Customer Contract with Netherby may not qualify as "Material" if below financial threshold, limiting warranty protection
- **Broad:** Contract clearly material given client's description as "key technology services provider," creating warranty breach

**Risk Rating:** Medium

```
"Material Contract" means any contract, agreement or arrangement:
(a) involving consideration or value in excess of £500,000 in any 12-month period;
(b) which is not terminable on 90 days' notice or less without penalty;
(c) which contains change of control, exclusivity or non-compete provisions; or
(d) which is otherwise material to the business, operations or financial condition of the Company.
```

**Direct Quote:** "the Company has not traded with Netherby Engineering Ltd... in the 12 months prior to the date of this Agreement"

**Legal/Commercial Consequences:**
- **Narrow:** Service arrangements may not constitute "trading," limiting warranty protection
- **Broad:** "Key technology services provider" relationship clearly constitutes trading, creating warranty breach

**Risk Rating:** Medium  
**Recommendation:** Clarify warranty to include all forms of commercial relationships

### 1. Material Customer Contract Change of Control Provision
**Issue:** Material Customer Contract contains change of control termination right contradicting Seller's warranty  
**Source:** [material_customer_contract.md] lines 55-56, [disclosure_letter.md] lines 29-33  
**Direct Quotes:**
- "Either party may terminate this Agreement on 30 days' written notice if the other party undergoes a change of control without the prior written consent of the counterparty. For the purposes of this clause, the counterparty is Netherby Engineering Ltd." (material_customer_contract.md lines 55-56)
- "For the purposes of Warranty 6.3 of the SPA, which states that no Material Contract contains a change of control provision that would be triggered by the transactions contemplated by the SPA, the Seller confirms that: There are no Material Contracts to which the Company is a party that contain any provision which would be activated, triggered or otherwise affected by reason of a change of control..." **Risk Rating:** High  
**Legal/Commercial Risk:** 
1. **Warranty Breach:** Seller's warranty (implied Warranty 6.3) is materially false
2. **Termination Risk:** Netherby Engineering Ltd could terminate the contract post-acquisition

**Recommended Action:**
1. Require Seller to obtain written consent from Netherby Engineering Ltd waiving change of control termination right
2. Amend disclosure letter to properly disclose the Material Customer Contract
3. Consider price adjustment or specific indemnity for risk of termination

**Issue:** SPA appears incomplete with missing clauses and definitions  
**Source:** [share_purchase_agreement.md] various, [disclosure_letter.md] references to non-existent clauses  
**Evidence:**

- Disclosure Letter references "Warranty 6.3" but no Clause 6 exists in provided SPA
- Missing clauses between 5.1(d) and 9.4 (clauses 6, 7, 8, and parts of 5 and 9)

**Risk Rating:** Medium  
**Legal/Commercial Risk:** Incomplete agreement creates uncertainty about parties' rights and obligations, particularly regarding:
1. Definition of "Material Contracts" (referenced but not defined)
2. Full scope of Seller's warranties
3. Indemnity provisions (only Clause 9.4 provided)
4. Other standard SPA provisions (tax, employees, etc.)

   - Completion accounts mechanism

**Source:** [share_purchase_agreement.md] line 83, [client_email.md] line 11  
**Direct Quotes:**

2. Investigate extent of trading relationship for proper disclosure
3. Consider impact on purchase price if relationship is material

**Formula:** Basket = Purchase Price × 1.0%
**Inputs:** Purchase Price = $160,000,000; Percentage = 1.0%

2. Multiply: $160,000,000 × 0.01 = $1,600,000
3. Compare to stated value: $1,600,000 = $1,600,000

**Recomputed Value:** $1,600,000
**Document Stated Value:** $1,600,000
**Discrepancy:** $0 (0%)

- Discrepancy: $0 (0%)

**Market Standard Comparison:** Typical basket is 0.5-1.0% of purchase price; 1.0% is at higher end favoring Seller

   - **Ambiguity:** Warranty states no trading, but client says key provider
   - **Risk:** Medium - potential warranty breach
   - **Action Required:** Clarify actual trading relationship
   - **Question for Client:** "Clarify extent of trading relationship with Netherby Engineering Ltd"

   - **Missing:** SPA lacks "Business Day" definition
   - **Risk:** Medium - ambiguity for notice periods and deadlines
   - **Action Required:** Include standard Business Day definition
   - **Recommended Amendment:** Add to Clause 1.1: "Business Day means any day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday in England"

### Low Risk Items

   - **Observation:** Purchase Price in USD, Material Contract in GBP
   - **Risk:** Low - but no conversion mechanism specified
   - **Action Required:** Consider adding exchange rate mechanism for cross-border payments
   - **Recommendation:** Add clause specifying exchange rate for GBP payments

2. **Obtain Netherby Consent:** Require Seller to obtain written waiver of change of control termination right

4. **Clarify Trading Relationship:** Resolve contradiction in Netherby trading warranty
5. **Define Business Days:** Add Business Day definition to SPA
6. **Review Full Disclosure:** Ensure all material contracts properly disclosed

7. **Monitor Regulatory Timeline:** Track merger clearance progress against deadlines

**Finding:** No Material Adverse Change clause identified in the provided SPA documents.

**Risk Assessment:** 
- **Risk:** Medium - absence of MAC clause limits Buyer's walk-away rights if material adverse change occurs between signing and closing
- **Market Standard:** Typical in UK private M&A transactions, especially for listed buyers
- **Favorability to Client:** Unfavourable - Buyer bears risk of adverse changes pre-closing

**Recommended Action:** 
1. Insert standard MAC clause allowing Buyer to terminate if Material Adverse Change occurs
2. Include standard carve-outs (industry-wide effects, changes in law, etc.) with "disproportionate effect" qualifier

**Proposed Amendment:** Add new Clause 4.2:
```
4.2 Material Adverse Change
(a) The Buyer may terminate this Agreement by written notice to the Seller if, prior to Closing, a Material Adverse Change occurs in relation to the Company.
(b) "Material Adverse Change" means any event, circumstance or change that has a material adverse effect on the business, operations, assets, liabilities, financial condition or prospects of the Company, taken as a whole, provided that none of the following shall constitute or be taken into account in determining whether there has been a Material Adverse Change:
(i) changes in economic, political, regulatory or market conditions generally affecting the industry in which the Company operates;
(ii) changes in law or accounting standards;
(iii) any matter disclosed in the Disclosure Letter;
(iv) any action taken by the Buyer or at its request;
(v) the announcement or pendency of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement;
(vi) any event, circumstance or change that affects the Company disproportionately less than other participants in the industry in which it operates.
```

## Material Adverse Change (MAC) Clause Analysis
**Finding:** No Material Adverse Change clause identified in the provided SPA documents.

**Risk Assessment:** 
- **Risk:** Medium - absence of MAC clause limits Buyer's walk-away rights if material adverse change occurs between signing and closing
- **Market Standard:** Typical in UK private M&A transactions, especially for listed buyers
- **Favorability to Client:** Unfavourable - Buyer bears risk of adverse changes pre-closing

**Recommended Action:** 
1. Insert standard MAC clause allowing Buyer to terminate if Material Adverse Change occurs
2. Include standard carve-outs (industry-wide effects, changes in law, etc.) with "disproportionate effect" qualifier

**Proposed Amendment:** Add new Clause 4.2:
```
4.2 Material Adverse Change
(a) The Buyer may terminate this Agreement by written notice to the Seller if, prior to Closing, a Material Adverse Change occurs in relation to the Company.
(b) "Material Adverse Change" means any event, circumstance or change that has a material adverse effect on the business, operations, assets, liabilities, financial condition or prospects of the Company, taken as a whole, provided that none of the following shall constitute or be taken into account in determining whether there has been a Material Adverse Change:
(i) changes in economic, political, regulatory or market conditions generally affecting the industry in which the Company operates;
(ii) changes in law or accounting standards;
(iii) any matter disclosed in the Disclosure Letter;
(iv) any action taken by the Buyer or at its request;
(v) the announcement or pendency of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement;
(vi) any event, circumstance or change that affects the Company disproportionately less than other participants in the industry in which it operates.
```
